metadata.title: AI's Speed Crash Is Creating the Next Opportunity
metadata.speaker: Jordi Visser (solo)

executive_takeaway: Highest-signal ideas: (1) Jordi declares the AI 'midcycle slowdown' is ending and calls this a sentiment/technical cleanse inside a structural bull market built on exponential token demand vs linear memory supply. (2) He is turning bullish again on memory semis (Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix) after cutting hard in May, citing shortages 'beyond 2030' and analyst estimates of Samsung 2026 operating profit >$217B. (3) He frames the recent AI selloff as a 'speed crash' (Samsung -21% 10-day, worst since COVID/Lehman) within a bull market, not a top. (4) Next theme = consumer AI agents ('far bigger than Opus 4.5'); coding agents were just the first token explosion; Goldman cited ~24x token upside. (5) He is launching a crypto-forward channel, arguing tokenization/stablecoins are US financial statecraft and 'Bitcoin is the S&P 500 of the future of tokenization.' (6) Macro: he expects the Fed (Warsh) to either hike once (25, 'one and done') or do nothing, with tailwinds for Bitcoin either way.

ai_workflows.name: Technical 'entry score' screen (Claude Co-Work)
ai_workflows.goal: Build a repeatable oversold/bull-market entry signal on his 100-name thematic portfolio
ai_workflows.tools: Claude Co-Work; updates files; 20-day % above, 50-day %, 200-day %; RSI; MACD
ai_workflows.approach: Track % of 100 names above 20/50/200-day and average RSI. Got to 21/100 above 20-day (oversold); bullish when >40% above 50-day and 200-day still rising (86/100). He says he'll show how to do it yourself by updating files in Claude Co-Work.
ai_workflows.why: Identifies sentiment/technical cleanse bottoms inside a structural bull market

ai_workflows.name: Long scarcity / short abundance framework
ai_workflows.goal: Separate winners from losers as AI commoditizes code
ai_workflows.tools: Mental model (no tool); applied to portfolio
ai_workflows.approach: Long anything physically constrained by linear humans that spenders are buying (memory, compute, power, Bitcoin). Short anything built on code replicable by a computer (SaaS/seat software like Salesforce).
ai_workflows.why: Encodes exponential token demand vs linear supply into a positioning rule

ai_workflows.name: Token-budget / model-choice discipline (from Dylan Patel)
ai_workflows.goal: Cut AI cost without cutting capability
ai_workflows.tools: Claude Code / Opus 4.5; cheaper models for workflows
ai_workflows.approach: Fixed workflows -> cheaper models; assistant-style work -> smartest model (fewer tokens, fewer iterations, less human time). Scale example: SemiAnalysis spend $100K (Nov) -> $4M (Jan) -> ~$11M annualized; peak week ~$14M for 90-person firm. Cut other SaaS/legacy spend, not AI.
ai_workflows.why: Jevons paradox: cheaper intelligence raises total usage; right model choice lowers effective cost

risks: Speaker is talking his book in part (owns Micron, Palantir, Bitcoin, silver; runs a 100-name thematic portfolio and an RIA/subscriber product).
He cut Micron hard in mid-May and is only now 'probably' buying back — entry timing uncertain; he admits he sold before the top unintentionally.
Comparisons to 2007 (mutual-fund behavior) and 'feeling a little like 2007' — he notes it could end like the first 10 days then; downside not ruled out.
Memory 'cyclicality' cut both ways: if you believe the cycle, the cheap PEG is a value trap (he acknowledges this explicitly).
Consumer-agent thesis depends on UX maturing (habit formation, trust, permissions) — explicitly 'coming soon,' not here.
Crypto call rests on Bessent's doctrine + GENIUS Act + agentic commerce; these are policy/regulatory dependent and partly aspirational.
He says Bitcoin is 'still a bear market technically' (below 50-day MA); needs >50-day then >200-day to confirm.
Capex numbers (SemiAnalysis $11.1T) are forecasts, not commitments; 'capex air pocket' risk he himself wrote about.
Open-source vs frontier split is presented with his lean; enterprise data (89% closed) could shift fast.
No specific price targets or position sizes beyond 'some'; concentrated basket = 10 names not individually disclosed (webinar July 15).
Claim that memory shortage persists 'beyond 2030' is a forecast sourced to industry quotes (Micron/SK Hynix/Dylan Patel), verify independently.

actionable_takeaways.item: Study the memory supply/demand gap (capacity +20-30%/yr vs demand doubling; shortages beyond 2030) before the next print
Build the oversold 'entry score' screen (%-above-20/50/200-day + RSI + MACD) on an AI basket; replicate via Claude Co-Work
Add consumer-AI-agent enablers (Apple, Meta, model labs) to watchlist; track interface/UX maturation as the trigger
Read Scott Bessent's NY Economic Club speech + Mohamed El-Erian op-ed on crypto as US financial statecraft
Validate the 'long scarcity / short abundance' framing against your own book; consider SaaS exposure
Watch the Fed hike-odds path into July; map both hike and no-hike scenarios to BTC
Independently verify SemiAnalysis $11.1T capex forecast and hyperscaler backlogs before treating as base case
